{{Quote|Hello, Furan. It's been a while.''"<br />"''Since just before the war. When you decided to frame my little social club.|Tahiri Veila and Furan|<ref name="Conviction" />}}
'''Furan''' was a [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Gangster/Legends|criminal]] of ill repute who operated just prior to the [[Second Galactic Civil War]]. However, the unsavory dealings of his [[Furan's social club|social club]] were brought to an end by [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Tahiri Veila]], and the Mon Calamari was sentenced to a [[Prison/Legends|prison]] term in the [[Armand Isard Correctional Facility]]. In [[44 ABY]], following the civil war, Furan chanced upon an opportunity to avenge himself when Veila was [[Trial of Tahiri Veila|sentenced]] to the same prison. Alongside several comrades, Furan [[Unarmed combat/Legends|confronted]] Veila but was soundly beaten by the former Jedi Knight.

==Biography==
{{Quote|Gaharrag, Leurm, look who we have here.|Furan meets Tahiri Veila in prison|<ref name="Conviction" />}}
[[File:Tahiri.jpg|thumb|right|180px|Tahiri Veila, whose intervention as a Jedi made Furan be convicted of grand vehicle theft.]]
Furan was a [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] active as a [[Gangster/Legends|criminal]] in the [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before the [[Second Galactic Civil War]]<ref name="Conviction" /> that started in [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]].<ref name="40 ABY">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of ''[[Legacy of the Force: Betrayal]]'', which include the beginning of the [[Second Galactic Civil War]], to [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]].</ref> Members of his [[Furan's social club|social club]] also engaged in criminality and joined the Mon Calamari in the [[Thief/Legends|theft]] of [[Army/Legends|army]] [[Medcenter/Legends|hospital]] [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttles]], the parts of which they stripped and sold illegally. Their lawlessness was brought to an end by the efforts of [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Tahiri Veila]], who discovered evidence that implicated Furan and an [[Furan's buddy|accomplice]] in the heists. The gangsters were charged with grand [[Starship/Legends|vehicle]] theft and were found guilty on the strength of the incriminating account given by Furan's partner, who [[Death/Legends|died]] soon afterward. Sentenced to [[Prison/Legends|prison]], Furan was committed to a term in the [[Armand Isard Correctional Facility]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. He made the acquaintance of many other criminals while incarcerated, among them two fellow [[Assassin/Legends|killers]]: [[Gaharrag]], an imposing [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]]; and a massive [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] named [[Leurm]].<ref name="Conviction" />

In [[44 ABY]],<ref name="ERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of ''[[Fate of the Jedi: Conviction]]'' to [[44 ABY]].</ref> an opportunity for vengeance arose for Furan when Tahiri Veila, who was no longer a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], was herself [[Trial of Tahiri Veila|sentenced]] to a term in the [[Armand Isard/Legends|Armand Isard]] Correctional Facility for her own crimes during the civil war. The Mon Calamari enjoyed a [[Time/Legends|time]] of recess when Veila was mistakenly brought to the same exercise yard occupied by the majority of the prison's male population&mdash;Furan included. He was the first of them to confront her, with accusations of evidence fabrication against his social club, only to be reminded of his late confederate's damning testimony.<ref name="Conviction" />

When it became apparent that she would not be intimidated, Furan summoned Gaharrag, Leurm, and several other prisoners to join him in the ex-Jedi's slaughter. Taunting ensued as the inmates prepared to [[Unarmed combat/Legends|attack]] her, but Veila preceded them with a perfectly-landed kick to the center of Furan's head, a deadly maneuver so sudden he was unable to cry out in pain before he collapsed. All of his allies were subsequently defeated by Veila, who was herself finally brought down with a high-intensity [[Stun/Legends|stun bolt]]. The prison's [[Unidentified Human warden|warden]] later told Veila that both Gaharrag and Leurm suffered broken [[Limb/Legends|limbs]], while Furan regained consciousness sometime later, the recipient of a violent concussion. The [[Warden/Legends|warden]] then scolded Veila for starting the fight by attacking Furan.<ref name="Conviction" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Fabricated evidence of grand vehicle theft against us.''"<br />"''Fabricated? You and your motor-pool buddy were stealing and chopping army hospital shuttles. My evidence didn't convict you. Your buddy's testimony did.|Furan accuses Tahiri Veila of setting him up|<ref name="Conviction" />}}
Furan was a [[Color/Legends|salmon-pink]]-skinned Mon Calamari male with prominently-displayed gang [[Tattoo/Legends|tattoos]] and kill silhouettes about his head and neck. He preferred to socialize with other unsavory [[Sentience/Legends|beings]] and made no qualms about his inherent delinquency. However, Furan was not one to take responsibility for his actions and was instead quick to reassign blame to beings other than himself, even going as far as making accusations of fabricated evidence against his social club. The felonious inclinations of his crime mob earned the ire of, and a bad reputation with, Tahiri Veila, a Knight of the [[New Jedi Order]]. When the two reconnected in the exercise yard of the Armand Isard Correctional Facility, it had been several years since their last encounter, and Furan still harbored much of the animosity he had initially felt for Veila when her intervention resulted in his arrest and ultimate conviction.<ref name="Conviction" />

==Skills and abilities==
{{Quote|You shouldn't&mdash;|Furan to Veila, before she kicked him in the face|<ref name="Conviction" />}}
Furan was capable of performing calisthenics. Tahiri Veila was more than a match for him in unarmed combat, a fact which was brought into sharp relief as the ex-Jedi made short work of Furan and his yard mates.<ref name="Conviction" />

==Equipment==
As an inmate at Armand Isard Correctional Facility, Furan wore a yellow [[Jumpsuit/Legends|jumpsuit]].<ref name="Conviction" />

==Behind the scenes==
Furan appeared in [[Aaron Allston]]'s [[2011]] novel ''[[Fate of the Jedi: Conviction]]'', the seventh installment of the nine-part [[Star Wars: Fate of the Jedi|''Fate of the Jedi'']] series.<ref name="Conviction" />
